comments.content: `role: "user" | "assistant"` is likely incomplete for an agentic flow that already models `tools` and `skillFailure`. Most agent backends emit a third message role carrying tool results (e.g. `"tool"`), which would currently be dropped or force every consumer to widen the union ad-hoc. Confirm with the backend SSE contract; if tool results are streamed as separate messages, add `"tool"` here (and consider a sibling field carrying the originating `toolCallId`).

All untrusted-string fields (`content`, `thinking`, `args`, `completedSummary`, and `reason` inside `SkillFailure`) are typed as opaque `string`. Nothing in this file establishes a boundary between raw model/tool output and rendered text, so XSS responsibility silently falls on every renderer. Since this is the central type module, add a doc comment here (or a branded alias) making the escape-at-render contract explicit, so reviewers can audit each consumer against it. This is documentation, but it lives on the type that every downstream file imports — the natural enforcement point.

UI streaming state is mixed into the persistent message shape via `streaming?: boolean`. The persisted DB row and the in-flight SSE rendering now share one type, so any renderer that needs to display a finished-but-just-flushed message has to remember to clear this flag, and there is no compile-time way to distinguish a "message that arrived fully" from "message still streaming". Split into a `StreamingMsg = Msg & { streaming: true }` overlay (or a separate runtime wrapper) so persistence and presentation don't share state.

Type names drop the all-caps acronym used in their source constants: `ApiProvider` should be `APIProvider` to align with `API_PROVIDER_OPTIONS`, and `UiFontSize` should be `UIFontSize` to align with `UI_FONT_SIZE_OPTIONS`. Keeping the acronym casing consistent makes the relationship between constant and type immediately obvious at every call site.

comments.existing_code: export type ApiProvider = (typeof API_PROVIDER_OPTIONS)[number]["value"];

comments.content: The doc-comment binds array index to slider/button position ("索引位置 = SettingsPage 滑块/按钮的档位"), but the array carries no explicit ordering field. Reordering or inserting entries will silently shift which option each step selects, and reviewers will not see the breakage in this file. Either add an explicit `order` (or rely on a separate ordered list consumed by the UI), or have the UI look up by `value` instead of array index. Also note that "标准" vs "small/standard/large/xlarge" mixes Chinese UI labels with English identifier values — that's fine, but worth confirming consumers do not compare against translated strings.

The literal types `ApiProvider` / `UiFontSize` exist only at compile time. If values come back from persisted settings, query params, or a backend without a guard, drift from this source-of-truth will not be caught and TypeScript will silently treat the string as `string` at the boundary. Consider exporting a runtime guard (e.g. an `isApiProvider` / `isUiFontSize` type-predicate over `API_PROVIDER_OPTIONS` / `UI_FONT_SIZE_OPTIONS`) so call sites can validate on read.

The declared return type `{ anchor: { x: number; y: number }; edge: Edge }` is structurally different from the exported `Anchor` interface, which is the flat `{ x: number; y: number; edge: Edge }`. Callers that assign the result to an `Anchor` variable or destructure `result.anchor.x` instead of `result.x` will be silently mis-wired. Either change the signature to return `Anchor` directly (and drop the `anchor` wrapper) or rename the wrapper property to something that does not collide with the `Anchor` type name.

`loadAnchor` blindly casts `JSON.parse(raw)` to `Anchor` with zero runtime validation. A corrupted or hand-edited localStorage value (missing `x`/`y`, non-numeric coordinates, or an unknown `edge` string such as `"bottom"`) will be returned as a valid `Anchor` and crash downstream consumers that destructure `{ x, y, edge }` or pass it through. `loadSize` at least validates numeric ranges; `loadAnchor` should mirror that with a shape check (typeof for x/y, and an `Edge` allow-list), otherwise persist a schema version key.

`export let widgetDragActive` is a live ESM binding, but consumers can still observe a stale value in two common React scenarios: (1) reading it once at module-init time into a `const`, or (2) reading it inside a stale closure/callback created before `setWidgetDragActive` ran (e.g. an event handler memoized without a re-read). Because the file's leading comment explicitly relies on cross-component visibility, make the contract safer by exporting a getter or, better, an object wrapper that always returns the current value: `export const widgetDragActive = { value: false };`. This removes the live-binding footgun while preserving the shared-module pattern the comment describes.

`screenSize` silently returns a hardcoded 1920x1080 on any failure with no logging, which will mask real issues (Tauri permission changes, headless CI, scaled multi-monitor setups, monitor API breakage across Tauri versions) and produce quietly wrong layouts. At minimum `console.warn` the caught error, and consider falling back to `window.innerWidth/innerHeight` (already in logical pixels) before resorting to the magic numbers.

`loadSize` validates against `PANEL_W_MIN/MAX`/`PANEL_H_MIN/MAX` imported at module-load time but never re-checks the saved value against the *current* monitor. Two real failure modes: (1) on a smaller display where `PANEL_W_MAX` was later reduced, a previously valid stored size is silently rejected and the widget falls back to defaults with no signal; (2) on a smaller display where the user later shrinks the constants, an over-large stored size could be loaded if the constants grow again. Tighten by clamping the loaded value to the current monitor size after the bounds check, so out-of-byscreen sizes get coerced rather than dropped.

`setTaskH` does not validate its input: passing `NaN`, `Infinity`, or a negative number will silently write `"NaNpx"` / `"-5px"` into `--task-h`. `getTaskH` masks `NaN` via `Number.isFinite` but a downstream `style.setProperty("--task-h", "NaNpx")` is a real footgun, especially since this helper is called from a Splitter drag handler that may compute intermediate values. Add a `Number.isFinite(h) && h >= 0` guard.

Optional props `archived` and `trashed` carry JSDoc explaining their UI effect, but `autoEdit?: boolean` is undocumented. Consumers / reviewers cannot tell what the default is, whether `false` means "do not auto-edit", or how it interacts with view/edit mode toggling. Add a brief JSDoc for consistency and to avoid misuse at call sites.

comments.content: onRetry callback has no error handling. If the retry throws (e.g., the re-invoked Tauri command raises a CommandError synchronously), the exception escapes unhandled — defeating the entire purpose of routing through `handleCommandError`. Wrap the call in try/catch and forward any error back through `handleCommandError(e, ctx, options)` (with `silent: true` to avoid double-alerting after a confirm).

Type guard is asymmetric in its drift defense. The JSDoc explicitly says `code` is kept as `string` so Rust can ship new codes ahead of the frontend, but `recoverable` is gated as a strict `boolean`. Any future Rust change that makes the field optional (`Option<bool>`), renames it, or omits it would silently fail the guard and route a real `CommandError` through the non-structured branch (no hint, no retry affordance). Either default `recoverable` to `false` on missing, or document the same lax-vs-strict split for `recoverable` that is documented for `code`.

`hintForCode` is a hand-maintained switch whose exhaustiveness is not enforced at compile time. Adding a new `CommandErrorCode` to the union (or to `ALL_COMMAND_ERROR_CODES`, or to Rust) without touching the switch silently routes the new code to `default: null` — the user loses the actionable hint and the codebase loses its drift-defence contract (the file header even claims `ALL_COMMAND_ERROR_CODES` is the sync source of truth). Add a `const _exhaustive: never = code as never;` line in `default` (typed against `CommandErrorCode`) so a missing case fails compilation, or replace the switch with a `Map<CommandErrorCode, string>` literal keyed off `ALL_COMMAND_ERROR_CODES`.

The collision-probability claim "< 1e-10" in the JSDoc is per-pair, not birthday-paradox adjusted. The fallback only emits a 6-char base36 suffix (~36^6 ≈ 2.18e9 space), and within the same millisecond the Date.now() prefix is constant, so the effective uniqueness domain is the random suffix alone. After roughly sqrt(2 * 36^6) ≈ 66k IDs generated in the same ms (or in fast succession), collision probability rises sharply. Either widen the suffix (e.g. slice(2, 14)) or — better — fall back to `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(8))` and base36-encode the bytes, which removes the statistical weakness without depending on `randomUUID`.

The `///` triple-slash style is Rust's outer-doc-comment syntax. In TypeScript these are parsed as ordinary `//` line comments (the leading `//` consumes the third slash), so they work but visually signal "this is special" to readers familiar with Rust, and most TS linters/formatters (eslint, prettier, dprint) won't recognize them as doc comments attached to the field. Use `//` or, preferably, JSDoc `/** ... */` so the comment is consistently attached to the `token` field and tooling treats it as documentation.

ProposalTarget discriminated union exposes snake_case fields (tool_name, skill_name, policy) that will appear on deserialized JSON objects. The header comment only describes camelCase→snake_case conversion for Tauri 2 command *parameters*; it does not address the response/read path, where these field names come back verbatim from serde. Consumers used to TS camelCase conventions may write `{ toolName: ... }` and silently get `undefined` at runtime even though the code type-checks. Consider either (a) extending the header comment to make the read-path contract explicit ("response payloads are NOT auto-converted — keep these fields snake_case on the TS side"), or (b) introducing a transform layer that maps to a camelCase TS-facing type so the rest of the codebase can use idiomatic names.

ApprovalSource mixes "actors/sources" (auto_applied, human_approved, system_rejected, human_rejected) with the lifecycle value "pending". An approval source of "pending" is semantically a state, not a source/actor — likely indicates either a backend serde enum bug or a domain-model mismatch worth surfacing before the TS surface locks it in. Verify against the Rust enum; if it really is intentional, rename the variant (e.g. split into ApprovalSource vs. an `awaiting` flag on ChangeRecord) so the type name matches its meaning.

ProposalStatus and ChangeStatus share the values `rejected` and `expired`, and ChangeStatus also adds `pending`, but nothing in this file documents which ProposalStatus transitions are legal once a proposal is promoted to a ChangeRecord. Future maintainers adding status logic may introduce invalid transitions that violate the backend contract. Consider a short JSDoc on each enum describing the lifecycle role (e.g. "Proposal lifecycle: pooled → promoted → ...", "Change lifecycle: pending → shadowing → ... → rolled_back"), or a typed transition table.

export type ProposalStatus = "pooled" | "promoted" | "expired" | "rejected";
comments.existing_code: export type ProposalStatus = "pooled" | "promoted" | "expired" | "rejected";

comments.content: Modifying native DOM prototype `Element.prototype.scrollTo` / `scrollIntoView` violates the project's prototype-chain-safety rule (only Array/Object were named, but Element is just as native). These assignments run at module load and persist across the entire test run, leaking into every spec. Prefer stubbing on the component under test, using `vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'scrollTo')`, or scoping the polyfill to the suites that actually need it.

The patched `console.error` is installed once at module load and never restored in `afterEach`. The captured `originalError` is only used as a fallback forward, so if later code (or another setup file) reassigns `console.error` the chain breaks silently, and our own filter outlives the test run. Also, `msg.includes("not wrapped in act")` will swallow any unrelated error whose message happens to embed that substring (e.g. third-party warnings), which can hide real regressions. Restore the original in `afterEach` and match a tighter pattern such as `/\bnot wrapped in act\b/` anchored at the start of the first arg.

Two `(globalThis as any)` casts disable `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` to silence the linter. The project rule forbids `any` without justification. Declare a minimal interface (e.g. `interface CryptoLike { randomUUID?: () => string }`) and cast through that, or assign to a properly typed module declaration so the linter stays happy without disabling it.

The fallback `if (typeof globalThis.crypto === "undefined") { (globalThis as any).crypto = {}; }` creates an empty crypto shim that only has `randomUUID` attached a few lines later. Any code that touches `crypto.getRandomValues`, `crypto.subtle`, etc. will throw a cryptic `TypeError: ... is not a function` instead of being properly polyfilled. Either remove this branch (let it fail fast so callers know crypto isn't supported) or polyfill `getRandomValues` with `node:crypto.webcrypto` / a `Uint8Array` filler so the shim is actually useful.

`Object.defineProperty(window, "matchMedia", { writable: true, value: vi.fn().mockImplementation(...) })` is invoked unconditionally, but it only has effect when `window.matchMedia` is missing. The mock itself is fine, however `vi.fn()` here is created once at module load and never reset; since the matchMedia mock object is reused across tests, any call-assertions would accumulate state. That's likely fine because nothing asserts on matchMedia calls, but if it ever is asserted on, `vi.restoreAllMocks()` in `afterEach` will revert the mock factory and the next call would receive an un-mocked implementation. Move the matchMedia mock into a `beforeEach` or recreate it with `vi.fn()` after restoration.

**Double-commit risk on Enter → Blur**: After `commit()` runs because of Enter, `cancelledRef.current` is reset to `false` but no flag is set to mark the "just-committed" state. If the input is still in the DOM when blur subsequently fires (e.g., `onCommit` sets `editing=false` but the batched re-render unmounts the input, during which React fires a synthetic blur), `onBlur` will call `onCommit(draft)` a second time with the same draft — a duplicate submission. The same can occur if Enter naturally causes focus to leave (e.g., implicit form submit). Consider introducing a symmetric `justCommittedRef` (set true at the top of `commit()`, cleared in `onBlur` after skipping) to guard against this — mirroring the cancellation pattern already used for Escape.

**`cancelledRef` state leak across edit sessions**: The flag is only cleared inside `commit()` and inside the cancelled branch of `onBlur`. If Escape causes the input to unmount along a path where blur never fires (e.g., parent unmounts before focus-out, focus is moved programmatically, or the input is replaced by a read view without losing DOM focus in a way React observes), `cancelledRef.current` stays `true` into the next edit session. The first blur (or even Enter, since `commit()` explicitly clears it so Enter would still commit) of the next session can then be silently suppressed. Reset the flag in the same effect that initializes the draft on entry to editing mode, so each session starts with a clean slate.

**Intentional `eslint-disable` for exhaustive-deps is fragile**: Suppressing the lint rule for `[editing]` only is correct (so an external `value` change doesn't clobber an in-progress draft), but this is exactly the kind of footgun a future maintainer may "fix" and reintroduce the draft-clobber bug. Consider extracting `value` into a ref snapshot taken when entering edit mode, and depend on `[editing]` only via that snapshot — it both makes the intent self-documenting in code and removes the need for the eslint-disable.

**`commit()` ordering: mutation before consumer callback**: `cancelledRef.current = false` runs before `onCommit(draft)`. If the consumer's `onCommit` throws synchronously, or synchronously re-renders the parent in a way that fires blur (which then sees `cancelledRef` already cleared and may re-call `onCommit`), the invariant becomes order-dependent. Either clear the flag after `onCommit` succeeds, or wrap in `try { onCommit(draft) } finally { cancelledRef.current = false }` so failure leaves the cancellation state intact. Minor, but worth tightening given how many subtle cases the E4 fix already addresses.

**Empty/unchanged draft handling is implicit**: Both Enter and Blur unconditionally forward `draft` to `onCommit`, including empty strings and drafts identical to `value`. For a title editor (TaskCardContent / TodoCard) this may allow accidental empty titles, or fire redundant parent updates on a no-op blur. Either guard against `draft.trim() === ''` here, or call out explicitly in the JSDoc that consumers are responsible for empty/duplicate filtering.

`raw.trim()` is forwarded verbatim to the Rust backend via `invoke("open_file_path", { path: target })` with no client-side hardening. `isAbsPath` only confirms the prefix matches the drive-letter/unix-root pattern — it does not reject NUL bytes, control characters, length anomalies, or non-canonical forms, and the user-supplied tail (after the prefix) is unconstrained. If the Rust command does not independently canonicalize and reject traversal/empty/oversized paths, this is the command-injection / arbitrary-file-open attack surface. Either tighten `isAbsPath` to verify the full token matches the same shape used by `LINK_OR_PATH_RE`, or have the frontend explicitly re-validate `target` against the path regex before invoking.

`isAbsPath` allocates a fresh `RegExp` on every call (`new RegExp(\`^${PATH_PREFIX}\`)`). All other patterns in this module are pre-built once and exported/used as constants. Hoist this to a module-level `const ABS_PATH_RE = new RegExp(\`^${PATH_PREFIX}\`)` so it matches the surrounding pattern and avoids per-call allocation, especially since `extractFilePaths` style callers may invoke it inside render loops.

Project rules prefer `async/await` over Promise chains. The two fire-and-forget branches use `.catch()` callbacks. Wrap each call in `async` and use `try { await ... } catch (e) { handleCommandError(...) }` — this is easier to read, easier to extend (e.g., adding telemetry), and consistent with the rest of the codebase's async style.

`force=true` is ignored when a load is already in flight. `if (cache && !force) return cache;` skips when `force` is true, but the subsequent `if (!loading)` is false (the previous non-forced load is still pending), so the function returns the stale in-flight promise instead of issuing a fresh fetch. Callers who explicitly request a refresh can receive the unforced result. Fix: when `force` is true, ignore `loading` and start a new invocation (and ideally cancel or chain off the previous one so subscribers still get a fresh value).

Setters `setProfileName`, `setProfileAvatar`, and `removeProfileAvatar` use `.then()` with no `.catch()`. A rejected invoke becomes an unhandled promise rejection, leaving `cache`/subscribers inconsistent with the backend and giving no user-visible feedback (unlike `loadProfile`, which routes failures through `handleCommandError`). Add `.catch` (or convert to `await` + try/catch) that surfaces the error, and do not call `notify()` on failure.

Setter `.then` handlers unconditionally overwrite `cache` and broadcast `notify()`. If a `profile-changed` event arrives from another window/挂件 after the invoke was issued but before it resolves (or vice-versa), the later write can clobber a fresher value with a stale snapshot, causing UI flicker and lost updates. Track a monotonic version/timestamp on each `ProfileView` and only apply a write when it is strictly newer than the current cache (the same guard should apply to the `profile-changed` listener).

`listen("profile-changed", ...)` is registered but the returned unlisten function is discarded, and there is no way to tear it down. The module-level `listening` flag prevents re-registration within the same module instance, but under Vite HMR or repeated module evaluation the previous listener leaks (Tauri holds a strong reference to the JS callback), and the new module instance will skip registration because `listening=true` was set before the listen promise resolved. If that first `listen` rejects (the `.catch(() => {})` swallows it silently) the module is permanently in a "broken, thinks it is listening" state. Store the unlisten function, call it on module dispose (e.g., `import.meta.hot?.dispose`), and treat a failed `listen` as not-listening so a future call can retry.

`ensureProfileListen()` is only invoked from `loadProfile`. If a consumer calls `setProfileName` (or relies solely on `subscribeProfile` + a pre-populated cache) before ever calling `loadProfile`, the `profile-changed` listener is never attached and cross-window updates are silently missed. Either always install the listener at module init (after first ensuring the Tauri runtime is available), or document and enforce a "call `loadProfile` first" contract for every consumer.

Additionally the `.then` has no `.catch`, so a rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Use a cancelled flag and assign the unlisten function synchronously when ready.

Either invoke a backend "skip"/"cancel" command or document explicitly that dismissing without confirmation is treated as "bind none".

comments.content: Concurrent event race against in-flight `confirm`. While `confirm` is awaiting `invoke('confirm_artifact_batch', ...)` with `busy === true`, a new `artifact-batch-ready` payload will overwrite `ready`/`selected` and clear `error` from inside the listener. The originally pending invoke then either: (a) succeeds and calls `setReady(null)` while the user is reviewing batch B, or (b) fails and the resulting `formatCommandError` is rendered against the unrelated payload B. comments.content: Both `onPointerDown` and `onClick` call `stopPropagation`. Stopping propagation on `pointerdown` already suppresses the synthesized `click` for most listeners, so the `onClick` stop is often redundant — but if the parent listens to `onMouseDown`/`onPointerDown` for drag/select, the double-stop is intentional and necessary. Confirm the parent's event wiring; if only `onClick` is used upstream, simplify to a single stop on the click handler to avoid masking future interaction regressions.

Async `listen()` registration is racy: `unlistenFn` is assigned only after the promise resolves, but the cleanup runs synchronously on unmount. If the component unmounts (or StrictMode tears down & remounts in dev) before `listen()` resolves, `unlistenFn` is still `undefined`, cleanup does nothing, and the listener gets registered afterwards with no cleanup ever firing — leaking a listener that will call `setPending`/`setRemaining` on an unmounted component (and double-registering under StrictMode). Fix: track an `unmounted` flag inside the IIFE and skip assigning/using the listener once unmounted, or move registration behind a cancellable promise.

Pending request is silently overwritten when a new `bot-confirm` event arrives before the user responds. The handler unconditionally `setPending(p)` and resets the timer, but never sends a response for the previous in-flight request — correctness then depends entirely on the backend's 60s fail-safe, breaking the widget's "one response per id" contract and violating the spec §12.7 widget contract. Either queue requests, or auto-deny the previous one (with a reason) before switching to the new one.

`respond()` is not reentrancy-safe: `if (!cur || busy) return;` reads the React state variable `busy`, but `setBusy(true)` is asynchronous and not committed until the next render. A rapid second call (double-click, or the countdown effect's `respond(false)` firing concurrently with a button click, or a new event arriving mid-invoke) can both observe `busy === false`, both call `invoke("bot_confirm_response", ...)`, and send duplicate/contradictory responses for the same `id`. Use a `useRef` mirror for the busy guard so the check and the set are both synchronous.

`pendingRef.current = pending;` is a write-during-render side effect, not a pure render. It also runs on every render — including when the component is in the middle of committing a different state — so the countdown's `respond(false)` can read a stale payload from the ref and act on the wrong `id`. Move it into a `useEffect` (or use the standard `useEffect(() => { ref.current = state }, [state])` pattern) so updates are committed deterministically.

If the active element is unmounted mid-drag (e.g. parent state change removes the task before `onDragEnd` fires), `active.rect.current` can be `undefined` and the property access throws before `onReorder` is ever called. Use optional chaining (`active.rect.current?.translated ?? active.rect.current?.initial`) and also guard `over.rect`'s `.top`/`.height` access, since dnd-kit sometimes reports `null` rects during a fast pointer release.

When the drop resolves with `over.id === active.id` (very common — dnd-kit will often pick the dragged card itself as `over`, especially on a same-column drop with no neighbour highlighted), the handler only commits when the draft already shows a cross-column change. Data integrity: `/clean` clears the UI (`setMessages([])`) **before** invoking `bot_history_clear`, and the persistence call is fire-and-forget with `silent: true` error handling. If the backend call fails, the user believes the session is empty but the backend still has the messages — the next `bot_history_load` (e.g. session switch / reload) silently resurrects the supposedly-deleted history. comments.content: `openDir` is the only action that neither guards on `busy` nor clears `setError("")` before running. Inconsistent with `importSkill`/`removeSkill` and allows the open call to interleave with an in-flight import/delete and leave a stale error visible after a successful open. Every catch block calls both `handleCommandError(e, name, { silent: true })` and `setError(formatCommandError(e))`, giving two independent code paths for the same failure. If the two helpers ever format/extract differently, console and inline UI will disagree. `refresh` is recreated every render but referenced from a `useEffect` with an empty dep array. Today it only touches setters so it works, but it hides any future state capture and triggers `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` lint. Wrap `refresh` in `useCallback` and include it in the deps, or inline the invoke so the effect's contract is obvious.

`removeSkill` relies on the browser-native `window.confirm`, which inside the Tauri WebView may render as a native OS dialog (or be blocked) and is inconsistent with the rest of the styled UI. Also, unlike `importSkill`, there is no success `notice` after deletion. Consider a custom confirm modal and a "技能「${name}」已删除" notice for parity.

The `source` whitelist in the comment doesn't match the actual guard. The comment says "source = Bot/Api/Migration: already persisted by backend, don't write back", but the code only exempts `"initial-load"` and `"migration"` from the upsert/delete branch and treats every other value (including `"bot"` / `"api"` / unknown strings) as writable. If the backend ever emits `tasks-updated` with `source: "bot"` (or any non-tabulated source), this code logs it as "unknown, treat as not-persisted" and then still runs `upsertTasks`/`deleteTaskRows` from a stale snapshot, causing double-write and clobbering backend timestamps (and breaking the RMW baseline you set via `t.expectedUpdatedAt`). Either tighten the guard to match the comment (e.g., exclude `bot`/`api`/`migration`), or correct the comment to reflect the implemented behavior.

Race condition between `mutate()` and concurrent `tasks-updated` events (and between two concurrent `mutate()` calls). All callers capture `prev = tasksRef.current` synchronously, then issue async `upsertTasks`/`deleteTaskRows`. During those awaits, a later event/mutate can fully complete (it reads the same stale `tasksRef`, computes its own `next`, persists, and writes tasksRef + setTasks). When the earlier `mutate()` finally finishes, it overwrites `tasksRef.current` and state with its now-stale `next`, so the widget's payload (or the user's later edit) is lost from memory even though both writes reached the DB — UI/db diverge until next reload. Suggested fix: serialize all writes through a single mutex (the same `queue = queue.then(...)` pattern used for `tasks-updated`), or compare-and-retry on the `updatedAt` baseline before committing `tasksRef.current = next`.

Silent partial-failure in `mutate`: `upsertTasks(upserts)` succeeds but `deleteTaskRows(deletes)` throws → mutate rejects, `tasksRef.current` / `setTasks` / `emit("tasks-changed")` are all skipped, and `mutateFire`'s `.catch` only `console.error`s. The DB ends up with the upserts committed but the deletes pending, the widget never receives `tasks-changed`, and the user has no indication anything went wrong. Consider catching the delete failure and either rolling back the upserts (best-effort), surfacing the error via `handleCommandError`, or at minimum still emitting `tasks-changed` so the widget reloads and resyncs.

The comment on `mutateFire` is misleading and hides a real UX gap. It states "错误已经由 storage 层 alert 提示用户，call site 只留 console 痕迹" — but `mutate` does not wrap `upsertTasks`/`deleteTaskRows` in a try/catch, so their rejections propagate straight to `mutateFire`'s `.catch`, which is `console.error` only. If persistence fails, the user sees no alert/dialog; they only see that the UI didn't update. Either remove the comment, or actually surface the error via `handleCommandError(e, "mutate persist", ...)` so the failure is visible.

`addTask` sets `editingId` synchronously after kicking off a `mutateFire` (fire-and-forget) that hasn't awaited persist yet. The new row isn't in `tasks` state when `setEditingId(id)` runs, so the editor may mount against a non-existent id and depend on a subsequent render after the upsert resolves. If `upsertTasks` rejects, `editingId` still points at a row that doesn't exist in state — `setEditingId(null)` is never called, and the editor can remain "stuck" looking for the id. Consider awaiting the persist (or exposing a callback) and only setting `editingId` once the row is known to be in state, and clearing it on persist failure.

`quick-add` listener uses `useEffect(..., [])` with `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` and captures the first-render `addTask`. Today it happens to work only because `addTask` reads `tasksRef` (stable) and calls setters; any future change that adds `useState`/props/derived deps to `addTask` will silently desync from the listener path. Either move `addTask` into the effect, use a ref to keep a current callback, or rewrite to `useCallback` and add it to the dep array.

Use of non-null assertion `mergedMap.get(t.id)!` is unsafe. `merged` is built from a Map that combined `tasksRef.current` with `upserts` and removed `deletes`; `next` is then `applyArchiveRule(applyTodayRule(merged))`. While in practice every id in `next` should also be in `merged`, any divergence (e.g., applyToday/applyArchive fabricating an id, or a bug in upstream mapping) becomes a hard TypeError that aborts the `tasks-updated` handler — and since it's inside the queued `handle`, the wrapped `.catch` will log but the merging logic for that event silently stops at the point of throw, leaving `tasksRef` in an intermediate state. Use a guard: `const prev = mergedMap.get(t.id); if (!prev) return false; return !taskEq(prev, t);`.

pickFile/pickFolder/removeFile/全部删除这些异步处理器在 await 期间捕获了 cur = taskFiles(task) 和 task 引用；如果用户在 Tauri 文件选择对话框停留期间另一个面板或机器人执行回调修改了 task.files（例如机器人完成任务清空了绑定文件），await 结束后仍然按旧 cur 合并新文件，并把旧 task.id 当作 onUpdate 目标——合并结果可能与当前 state 不一致、产生幽灵文件（再次保存时被 filesPatch 整个替换，丢失机器人刚写入的更新）。建议在 await 后重新读取 task 的最新引用（或用 functional updater：把 mergeFiles(cur, added) 后的新列表作为 patch 传给 onUpdate 时用最新的 task.files 做基线，而不是闭包里的 cur）。

comments.content: Header comments contain internal project chatter ("老板 16:05 拍板", "EvolutionPanel 改造，原按钮点击模式 → 图示 toggle 模式") rather than durable design intent. This kind of commentary should live in PRs/commits/changelogs, not source files — replace with concise, durable doc comments describing the component's contract.

**Stale closure over `sub.text` in the commit callback.** The `onCommit` passed to `useInlineEdit` closes over `sub.text`, so if the parent re-renders with a new `sub.text` (e.g. remote sync, undo, or another row's edit affecting shared state) while this row is in edit mode, the `text !== sub.text` comparison runs against the original value. Result: a legitimate save can be dropped (text equals stale sub.text even though it differs from the fresh value) or a no-op save can be forwarded. Track `sub.text` via a ref that is updated on every render and read the fresh value inside the commit callback.

**Click events still bubble from the checkbox and delete button.** `stop` only cancels `onPointerDown` to defuse the drag handle; it does not cancel `onClick`. If the parent `TodoCard` also binds `onClick` to enter card-level edit mode (alongside a pointerdown-drag guard), clicking the checkbox to toggle `done` OR clicking `x` to delete will ALSO trigger that card-level handler, producing double actions and a race between the row action and the card action. Same concern applies to the editing `<input>` and the text span used to enter edit mode. Add `onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}` next to `onPointerDown={stop}` on each of these four elements.

comments.content: Keyboard drag is unreachable: useSortable's `attributes` (which include `role="button"`, `aria-roledescription`, `aria-pressed`, and `tabIndex`) are spread on the wrapper div, while the actual drag `listeners` (including the KeyboardSensor activation) are passed via the render prop to a child. In the caller this child is a `` (`☰`), which is not focusable by default and does not receive the `tabIndex` from `attributes`. Result: a screen reader announces the whole card as a sortable button, but a keyboard user can never focus or activate the actual handle to start a keyboard drag. Fix: forward `attributes` (or at minimum `attributes.tabIndex` + `attributes.role` + `attributes["aria-roledescription"]`) to the same element that receives `listeners`, e.g. change the render-prop signature to `children: (handleProps: DraggableSyntheticListeners & DraggableAttributes) => ReactNode` and spread `handleProps` on the handle, leaving the wrapper without `attributes`.

comments.content: `it` is an opaque one-letter prop name in a public-ish component interface. It carries no meaning to readers and is easy to confuse with `id`/`item` in JSX. Consider renaming to `item` (the type is already `WorkspaceItem`) and updating the caller in `WidgetApp.tsx` accordingly.

Memory leak / stale closure: window listeners are attached inside `onDown` and only removed by the drag-end `cleanup` closure. If the component unmounts mid-drag (route change, conditional render, parent re-render that removes the bar, etc.), `pointermove`/`pointerup`/`pointercancel` stay bound to `window`, the captured `move` keeps invoking `onSplit` on a stale parent, `setWidgetDragActive(false)` is never called, and `el.releasePointerCapture` is never invoked. Track the listener handles in a ref and register an unmount cleanup (e.g., a `useEffect(() => () => …, [])`) that force-ends any active drag.

Pointer ID not validated for the window-level listeners: `setPointerCapture` is only honored for events routed through the captured element, but `move`/`cleanup` are bound to `window`, which receives pointer events from every active pointer (touch with a second finger, stylus + mouse, etc.). A stray pointer will update `acc` and `onSplit`, and the first `pointerup` from any pointer will tear down the active drag. Guard with `if (ev.pointerId !== e.pointerId) return;` in both handlers, and ideally bind listeners with `{ capture: true }` plus the `pointerId` filter rather than relying on pointer capture alone.

Unsafe cast on `e.target`: `(e.target as HTMLElement).closest("button")` assumes a non-null `HTMLElement`. `EventTarget` can be `null` on synthesized events, and even when defined it may be an `SVGElement`/text node, which does not have `HTMLElement.closest`. A null/undefined target will throw and bypass the intended early-return that lets the ▲/▼ buttons receive their `onClick`. Narrow the type with `if (e.target instanceof HTMLElement && e.target.closest("button")) return;` before the cast.

comments.content: Drag deltas use the same sign convention as the arrow buttons only by convention: ▲ → `onArrow(-40)` (chat bigger), ▼ → `onArrow(+40)` (task bigger), and `move` forwards positive `inc` when the pointer moves down. This contract is invisible from the file alone and is easy to break in the parent (e.g., negating `delta` for one of the two callbacks). Either document the sign convention on the `onSplit`/`onArrow` prop types (e.g., `onSplit: (deltaY: number) => void` with a JSDoc), or normalize both paths through a single helper so the two surfaces cannot drift.

runExport / runImport / runExportWs / runImportWs are `try/finally` with no `catch`. If `onExportTasks` / `onImportTasks` (or the workspace variants) reject, the spinner clears and the rejection is left as an unhandled promise — no error state is shown, so failures look indistinguishable from a successful no-op export/import. Add `catch (e) { setBotError(formatCommandError(e)); }` (or a dedicated `exportError`/`importError` state) so users actually see why the action failed.

`consolidateNow` calls `await loadConfig()` after the backend returns. `loadConfig` does an unconditional `setConfig(...)` with the backend's whole view (modelsByProvider, activeModelId, uiFontSize, allowedDirs, hasApiKey, key statuses, …). `consolidateBusy` does **not** gate `saveConfig`, and any in-flight edits the user made on a `ModelRow` / `uiFontSize` / `allowedDirs` / typed-but-not-yet-saved key while consolidation was running are silently overwritten — `loadConfig` does no merge. Either fetch only `lastRunAt` (or pass `{ skipReload: true }` and patch `lastRunAt` into local state) so concurrent local edits are preserved.

The transient-feedback `setTimeout`s for `setConfigSaved` / `setCopied` / `setConsolidateMsg` are never cleared. If the user navigates away from `SettingsPage` during the 1500–4000 ms window, the timer fires `setState` on an unmounted component (React warning) and, worse, a freshly mounted `SettingsPage` instance can be clobbered by the late timer. Store each timer id in a `useRef` and clear it in a `useEffect` cleanup, or wrap each flag in a small `useEffect` keyed off the trigger.

comments.content: The `onCommit` and `onCancel` inline arrows passed to `useInlineEdit` are recreated on every render. If `useInlineEdit` registers them in any effect/memo dependency array (a common pattern for editable hooks), this will trigger spurious re-runs and stale-closure bugs (e.g., a stale `onCommitTitle` being called after a parent re-render). Wrap with `useCallback` (or pass stable props if the hook supports it).

`const stop = (e: React.PointerEvent) => e.stopPropagation();` is re-allocated on every render. It is currently only consumed by inline handlers so it has no effect today, but it is a foot-gun: if anyone later passes it as a prop to a memoized child (DoneCircle, FoldToggle, ActorAvatar, subtask checkboxes, file chips, etc.), the new identity will defeat `React.memo` on those children. Wrap it in `useCallback` so identity is stable.

comments.content: In-place mutation of state objects. `byId.get(id)` returns references to the items currently held in state, and `changed.forEach((it) => (it.updatedAt = now))` mutates those references. Combined with `assignInsertOrder(arrayMove(...).map(id => byId.get(id)!))` where `assignInsertOrder` may also rewrite `order`, this mutates the live state objects outside of `setItems`. Treat `next` as immutable: build a fresh array (e.g. `next.map(it => ({ ...it, order: ..., updatedAt: now }))`) or have `assignInsertOrder` return new objects.

Two divergent update paths. Other mutations (`commitTitle`, `toggleCollapsed`, `updateLinks`, `addItem`, `commitAddLink`) go through `persist()`, which encapsulates state update + DB write + broadcast in one place. `handleSortEnd` reimplements all three steps inline with slightly different behavior (no `await`, different change-set tracking, mutations on items). Route the sort through `persist(next)` after computing `next` (or a thin `persistChanged(changed)` helper) to keep error handling, ordering of `setState`/`await`/`emit`, and observer invalidation consistent.

Reload can clobber optimistic state. Both `persist` and `handleSortEnd` emit `workspace-changed`, and the `listen("workspace-changed", reload)` handler inside this same component calls `loadWorkspaceFromDb().then(setItems)`. If a concurrent edit (other window, mounted widget) or a slower write races, the reload can land between `setItems(next)` and `upsertWorkspaceItems(next)` resolving, overwriting the local optimistic state with stale DB content. Either (a) skip reload when the local sequence number matches, (b) have `persist` not re-emit when the change came from this very component, or (c) pass a payload identifying the origin so the listener can ignore self-emitted events.

Silent persistence failures across all update paths. `upsertWorkspaceItems` / `deleteWorkspaceRows` are awaited without try/catch and without surfacing the error — only `pickLocal` routes errors through `handleCommandError`. A failed SQLite write leaves the optimistic UI showing a successful change while the DB diverges (and the subsequent `workspace-changed` reload then snaps the UI back to the old data, masking the failure). Wrap each persistence call (or the central `persist` helper) with try/catch + `handleCommandError` and roll back the optimistic state on failure.

`kind` is not re-derived when `targetUri` changes. `commitAddLink` recomputes the kind via `looksLikeUrl(targetUri)`, but `commitEditLink` blindly preserves the original link's `kind`. Editing a URL into a local path (or vice versa) leaves a stale kind, which means wrong icon and a misleading `linkDisplayName` fallback (URLs fall back to the full URI instead of the basename). Mirror the same `looksLikeUrl` classification here.

Fire-and-forget listener teardown. `const unlisten = listen(...); return () => { unlisten.then(f => f()); }` neither awaits the registration nor the cleanup, so (a) if the component unmounts before `listen` resolves, the listener can still be registered and is never unsubscribed, and (b) the unsubscribe is dispatched asynchronously after unmount, making teardown order non-deterministic under fast mount/unmount cycles. Switch to the modern async effect pattern: store the promise, await it in setup, and store the unsubscribe fn via `.then(f => { unlistenFn = f; return () => f(); })` so cleanup is synchronous once registration has settled.

Pervasive inline mutation of state for timestamps. Aside from the sort path noted above, `commitTitle`, `toggleCollapsed`, `updateLinks`, and `commitAddLink` all build a new outer array but pass references to inner `it` objects (only spreading the field that changes). That is actually safe here, but combined with the sort-path mutation it creates an inconsistency: same data is treated as immutable in some call sites and mutable in others. Recommend freezing the convention: every setter does `{ ...it, updatedAt: now, ...rest }`.
Nested ternary chain (3+ levels) violates the project rule 'Nested ternary expressions are not allowed'. Replace with a lookup map keyed by `edge`.
Nested ternary chain in the `list` derivation. Convert to an if/else block (or a lookup function returning a Task[]) to comply with the 'no nested ternary' rule.

The user wants a project-level summary of a full-repo scan based on 1146 comments across 237 files. Let me analyze the comments to identify cross-cutting patterns and the most important findings.

Let me categorize the issues I see:

1. **Tauri configuration/security issues**:
   - `$HOME/**` glob in capabilities/default.json grants opener permission over entire user home directory
   - `$APPDATA/**` exposes app-data of every program
   - `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` enabled in CSP
   - macOS code-signing config is placeholder
   - devCsp is malformed (missing semicolon)
   - `bundle.targets` has dmg at root instead of under macOS
   - No top-level `version` field in tauri.conf.json

2. **Concurrency/async issues** (very prevalent):
   - Mutex poisoning silently recovered via `e.into_inner()` in many places
   - Blocking std::fs operations inside async contexts
   - std::sync::Mutex held across async .await points
   - TOCTOU races throughout (many files)
   - Lock-poisoning recovery patterns that mask real bugs

3. **Error handling issues** (very prevalent):
   - `Result<_, String>` flattening errors at boundaries
   - `e.to_string()` losing error context
   - `let _ = ...` discarding results
   - `unwrap_or_else(|_| default)` masking real errors
   - Silent failure paths

4. **Database/SQLite issues**:
   - Non-atomic writes
   - TOCTOU races in optimistic concurrency
   - Missing transactions
   - Lock-poisoning recovery
   - JSON serialization fallback to `[]`

5. **Security issues**:
   - SSRF protections bypassable
   - Path traversal
   - Symlink escapes
   - API key storage in plaintext fallback
   - Token/credential handling
   - Log injection (model-controlled strings)

6. **Test/audit script issues**:
   - Hardcoded paths to /Users/renshi/Projects/wmessage/...
   - Module-level read_text() without error handling
   - Brittle regex/positional matching
   - Tests coupling to specific Chinese error messages

7. **TypeScript/React issues**:
   - Stringly-typed enums (e.g. "low"/"high"/"medium")
   - `as any` casts
   - Missing keyboard accessibility
   - Missing aria attributes
   - Memory leaks (uncleaned listeners, unbounded Maps)
   - Stale closures
   - Fire-and-forget listeners

8. **Vendored tiny_http issues**:
   - Many `unwrap()` in production paths
   - Unbounded header reading
   - Unimplemented functions
   - Old rustls/openssl versions

9. **Memory subsystem issues**:
   - Embedding failures collapse to None
   - Tag codec not round-trip safe
   - Hot path does two full-table scans per insert

10. **Configuration management issues**:
    - Magic strings duplicated
    - Multiple sources of truth for same enum
    - Theme/preference handling
    - IPC string keys

Let me write this up now.

### Top Issues

1. **Capability/CSP over-permissioning (`src-tauri/capabilities/default.json`, `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`)** — `$HOME/**` and `$APPDATA/**` globs grant the opener reach over the entire user filesystem and every other app's data directory; `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` is enabled in both dev and prod CSP; `devCsp` is malformed (missing semicolon), which folds `style-src` into `img-src`. These are the highest-leverage items because they affect every release build.

2. **Pervasive silent mutex-poisoning recovery** (`src-tauri/src/api_handlers/*.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_skills/state.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_skills/runtime.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_chat.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_py.rs`, `src-tauri/src/db/*.rs`, `src-tauri/src/memory/*.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/*.rs`) — `unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())` is used to "recover" from poisoned locks, with no logging or instrumentation. A previous thread panic mid-critical-section means the protected state is potentially inconsistent, and this pattern silently proceeds. This is the single most repeated root-cause across the codebase.

3. **Blocking std I/O inside async/Tauri commands** (`src-tauri/src/api_handlers/body.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot/*.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/*.rs`, `src-tauri/src/migration/*.rs`, `src-tauri/src/memory/store.rs`, `src-tauri/src/migration/commands.rs`) — Synchronous `std::fs::*` calls executed directly from `async fn` tauri commands (`evolution_panel/commands.rs`, `migration_commands`, `memory_consolidate`, `ocr.rs`, `bot/config/io.rs`). The async runtime is stalled for the duration; concurrent commands serialize behind the blocking syscall.

4. **`std::sync::Mutex` held across `.await`** (`src-tauri/src/app_state.rs`, `src-tauri/src/api_handlers/handlers.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_chat.rs`) — Both `app_state.rs` accessors hand out `&std::sync::Mutex` without type-level enforcement, and `api_handlers/handlers.rs` calls `req.respond(...)` while holding `API_RMW_LOCK` for the duration of slow-client I/O. This stalls an entire async worker thread.

5. **`Result<_, String>` as the universal error type** (`src-tauri/src/error.rs`, `src-tauri/src/db/*.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot/*.rs`, `src-tauri/src/eval/*.rs`, `src-tauri/src/migration/*.rs`, `src-tauri/src/memory/*.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/*.rs`, `src-tauri/src/py/*.rs`) — `e.to_string()` at every module boundary destroys structured error chains. Combined with `From<String>` blanket impls in `error.rs`, real domain errors collapse to `INTERNAL`, non-retryable. This is the most repeated anti-pattern, and the error.rs design explicitly defeats its own goals.

6. **Non-atomic writes to user-data JSONL/JSON files** (`src-tauri/src/bot/config/io.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot/config/schema.rs`, `src-tauri/src/db/migrations.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/change/record.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/candidate/entry.rs`, `src-tauri/src/sandbox/io.rs`, `src-tauri/src/panel/commands.rs`, `src-tauri/src/profile.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/activation.rs`, `scripts/sync-version.mjs`) — `std::fs::write` truncates in place across many critical files (`bot-config.json`, evolution JSONL, profile.json, etc.). A crash, panic, or disk-full mid-write leaves the file empty/truncated; on reload serde falls back to `Default()`, silently wiping user config (including `allowedDirs`, `bypass_llm`, API keys that haven't migrated to keyring yet).

7. **TOCTOU races on shared state** (`src-tauri/src/api_handlers/commands.rs`, `src-tauri/src/api_auth.rs`, `src-tauri/src/db/tasks.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot/config/schema.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_artifacts.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_skills/files.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_fs.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_chat.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_slash.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/candidate/mod.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/panel/commands.rs`, `src-tauri/src/due_notify.rs`, `src-tauri/src/migration/journal.rs`, `src-tauri/src/migration/run.rs`, `src-tauri/src/db/migrations.rs`) — Same shape in many places: read snapshot, decide, write — with no compare-and-set or transaction. `db_upsert`'s SQL-level `WHERE updated_at` guard silently no-ops on conflict with no caller-visible signal, and `SCHEMA_MIGRATION_CHECKED` in `bot/config/schema.rs` is a global AtomicBool that doesn't actually gate the read-modify-write.

8. **Log injection via model/tool-controlled strings** (`src-tauri/src/audit.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_model_loop.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_slash.rs`, `src-tauri/src/audit.rs`, `src-tauri/src/py/audit.rs`, `src-tauri/src/api_handlers/ratelimit.rs`) — `truncate_for_log` only bounds length; newlines, pipes, ANSI escapes, BEL, and backspaces pass through. A jailbroken model or hostile tool output can forge additional audit-log lines, and rate-limit log sanitization is explicitly incomplete. The audit subsystem is the explicit "integrity guarantee" and this directly undermines it.

9. **Long-running task lifecycle leaks** (`src-tauri/src/bot_chat.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_slash.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_scheduler.rs`, `src-tauri/src/due_notify.rs`, `src-tauri/src/exec_steps.rs`, `src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, `src-tauri/src/migration/commands.rs`, `src-tauri/src/migration/run.rs`) — Spawned tasks drop their `JoinHandle` immediately. `start_scheduler`, `start_due_notifier`, `bot_scheduler` loops have no shutdown signal; panics inside the loop die silently. `set_bot_assigned(app, &task.id, true)` paired with the false-set only on the Ok return path means a panic leaves the task permanently "assigned".

### Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Async-on-async runtime mistakes** (representative: `src-tauri/src/bot_skills/runtime.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/panel/commands.rs`, `src-tauri/src/migration/commands.rs`, `src-tauri/src/memory/consolidate.rs`, `src-tauri/src/ocr.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_fs.rs`) — Blocking `std::fs::*` inside `async fn`, `tauri::async_runtime::block_on` from a sync caller that may itself be on a tokio runtime, `JoinHandle` dropped so task panics vanish, mutex held across `.await`.

- **Silent error-swallowing primitives** (representative: `src-tauri/src/api_handlers/ratelimit.rs`, `src-tauri/src/audit.rs`, `src-tauri/src/error.rs`, `src-tauri/src/db/tasks.rs`, `src-tauri/src/migration/recovery.rs`, `src-tauri/src/memory/store.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot/config/io.rs`, `src-tauri/src/platform/copy_file.rs`) — The patterns `let _ = ...`, `unwrap_or_default()`, `.ok()?`, `unwrap_or_else(|_| default)`, `if let Ok(...)`, and `format!("...{e}")` appear dozens of times across every subsystem. They share the root cause: error context discarded at module boundaries.

- **Race conditions of identical shape** (representative: `src-tauri/src/db/tasks.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_artifacts.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_skills/files.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot/config/schema.rs`, `src-tauri/src/api_handlers/commands.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/panel/commands.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/candidate/mod.rs`, `src-tauri/src/migration/journal.rs`, `src-tauri/src/migration/run.rs`, `src-tauri/src/due_notify.rs`, `src-tauri/src/ocr.rs`) — `read snapshot → decide → write` without compare-and-set, transaction, or file lock. The same hazard is documented with different specifics in roughly 20+ files.

- **Stringly-typed enums where a typed enum would be checked at compile time** (representative: `src-tauri/src/bot_skills/parse.rs` (`risk_level`/`mode`/`rollback` as `String`), `src-tauri/src/db/skill_out.rs` (`kind: String`), `src-tauri/src/migration/types.rs` (`op: String`, `action: String`), `src-tauri/src/intent_router.rs` (raw keyword substrings), `src-tauri/src/error.rs` (wire-format strings triplicated), `src/components/SettingsPage/constants.ts` (literal types with no runtime guard), `src-tauri/src/memory/rank.rs` (`m.kind == "lesson"`)).

- **Stringly-typed IPC / config keys** (representative: `index.html` `localStorage` `"wmessage-theme"`, `src/theme.ts`, `src/profile.ts`, `src/components/WidgetApp/constants.ts` `SIZE_KEY = "***"`, `src/storage.ts` `STORAGE_KEY = "***"`, `src/components/WidgetApp/storage.ts`) — Magic strings duplicated in 2+ places; drift is silently absorbed as default-light-mode fallback.

- **Tests coupled to internal error wording** (representative: `tests-audit/audit_*.py`, `src-tauri/src/memory/tests.rs`, `src-tauri/src/migration/mod.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot_skills/manage.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/change/status.rs`, `src-tauri/src/audit.rs`) — Assertions do `e.contains("不能为空")` / `line.contains("ERROR")` / `msg.contains("合并")` / `count(">=").contains("中文")` — they break on every i18n or copy edit without surfacing the real regression.

- **Accessibility gaps in React components** (representative: `src/components/ChatPanel/Fold.tsx`, `src/components/ChatPanel/RichText.tsx`, `src/components/SettingsPage/ApiProviderSelect.tsx`, `src/components/SettingsPage/ModelRow.tsx`, `src/components/TodoCard/SubtaskRow.tsx`, `src/components/EvolutionPanel/EvolutionPanel.tsx`, `src/components/DoneCircle.tsx`, `src/components/FoldToggle.tsx`, `src/components/EvolutionPanel/DeleteConfirmDialog.tsx`, `src/components/WidgetApp/SortableWorkspaceCard.tsx`, `src/components/WidgetApp/SortableTaskCard.tsx`, `src/components/Toggle/Toggle.tsx`) — Missing `type="button"`, no `aria-expanded`, missing keyboard sensor, no `aria-controls`, modal without focus management, `role="radio"` absent on radiogroups.

- **Vendored tiny_http has many unaddressed upstream bugs** (`src-tauri/vendor/tiny_http/src/{connection,request,client,lib,response,util/*,ssl/*}.rs`) — Combined with `Cargo.toml` patch, this means every release binary carries the unmodified upstream.

- **AI / prompt-injection vectors** (representative: `src-tauri/src/bot_plan.rs` `fail_reason` verbatim into Replanner prompt, `src-tauri/src/audit.rs` log-injection, `src-tauri/src/evolution/trace.rs` parallel `TraceOutcome::Aborted` and `was_aborted: bool`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/proposal.rs` `DefaultHasher` for dedup) — The model is treated as an honest producer in many places.

### Quick Wins

1. **Centralize the magic IPC/storage keys** (`src/theme.ts`, `src/profile.ts`, `src/storage.ts`, `src/components/WidgetApp/constants.ts` `SIZE_KEY = "***"`, `index.html`) — replace the `"***"` placeholder and `"wmessage-theme"` duplication with a single exported `KEYS` module.

2. **Replace every `unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())` with `let guard = match lock.lock() { Ok(g) => g, Err(p) => p.into_inner() };`** and route the original `PoisonError` payload into `tracing::error!` (or `eprintln!` for now) — this is a one-liner per site but yields observability of every prior-panic-across-lock event.

3. **Wrap every `std::fs::write`/`std::fs::read_to_string` on critical JSONL/JSON (`bot-config.json`, `evolution-*.jsonl`, `profile.json`, `journal.jsonl`) in a `write_atomic(path, |f| writeln!(f, ...))` helper that uses `tempfile::NamedTempFile::persist`** — single change to a shared util, fixes 12+ sites at once.

4. **Replace `Result<T, String>` at module boundaries with `Result<T, crate::error::CommandError>`** (representative: `db/tasks.rs`, `db/skill_out.rs`, `bot_skills/{state,vars,parse,manage}.rs`, `memory/{store,embed,mod}.rs`, `migration/*`, `evolution/*`, `eval/*`) — and remove the `From<String> for CommandError::Internal` blanket in `error.rs`. This is the highest-impact change in the codebase.

5. **Add `tracing::instrument` + sanitize at every `append_*` audit sink** (`src-tauri/src/audit.rs`, `src-tauri/src/py/audit.rs`) — strip `\n` / `\r` / `| ` / ANSI escapes on top of the existing length cap. One helper, used in 6 call sites.

6. **Lock down `src-tauri/capabilities/default.json`** — replace `$HOME/**` and `$APPDATA/**` with `$HOME/.wmessage/**` and `$APPDATA/com.wmessage.app/**` (or the real bundle id), split `main` and `widget` windows into separate capability sets.

7. **Add `@vitest/coverage-v8` to `package.json` devDependencies** — referenced by `test:coverage` script and currently missing.

8. **Add `aria-expanded` + `type="button"` + `aria-controls`** to every component listed under accessibility in the cross-cutting section — these are mechanical, ~5–10 minute fixes each.

9. **Replace `new RegExp` per call in `src/lib/openTarget.ts`** with a hoisted module-level `const ABS_PATH_RE` — and similarly fix all `path_openable_in`/`regex::new` per-call hot paths in `bot_skills/parse.rs` and `intent_router.rs`.

10. **Add a one-shot `expect_versions_match` test that asserts the rendered emoji/wording in `prompts/{consolidate,planner,summary,mod}.rs` matches the parser in `bot_skills/parse.rs` and the regex in `evolution/derive.rs`** — eliminates ~30 substring-test brittleness sites.
